# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟 🖖 🖐 🤙 👏 ✌ 🖐 🤙 🤏 🤌 👏 🖐 🖖 🤟 🤙 🖐 ✌ 👏 🤙 🖐 ✌ 🤙 🤟 👏 🤟 ✌ 🤙 🖖 🖐 👏 🤙 ✌ 🖖 🤟 🤙]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

I can see a six-digit display, a red indicator light, and five wires in this order: red, purple, orange, green, yellow. I am sending these exact observations to the Blind, who can act on the bomb, and to the Mute, who can match them against the manual. The gestures received so far do not have an established meaning I can safely decode.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="The display reads 6. The indicator light is red. The wires from left to right are: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see display 6, red light, and wires left to right: 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow. Use the manual to determine the required action and signal it clearly.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟]

The bomb’s visible state is unchanged. Mute has now sent six identical 🤟 gestures to me. I cannot safely assign them a meaning, so I am relaying the exact count and symbol to Blind, along with the bomb readings already provided.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute just signaled six repetitions of the hand sign 🤟. I do not know its meaning. Bomb remains: display 6, red light, wires 1 red, 2 purple, 3 orange, 4 green, 5 yellow.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 🤟 👇 👇 👇]

Mute has added three 👇 gestures after the six 🤟 gestures. Since the bomb display is 6, this most plausibly encodes “for 6, use 3” — likely wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. I am relaying both the exact signal and the inferred action; Blind should rely on the manual’s rule before acting.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's complete signal is 🤟 repeated 6 times, then 👇 repeated 3 times. Likely instruction: for display 6, act on wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. Verify against the manual before cutting or manipulating it.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [6]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[orange] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 👇 👇]

Mute has repeated the three 👇 gestures, confirming the second part of the earlier signal. Together with the six 🤟 gestures already received, this indicates the manual’s instruction is to use wire 3. The third wire is orange. I am sending Blind the confirmation, without claiming that any action has been taken.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated 👇 three times, confirming the instruction: use wire 3. Wire 3 is orange. No bomb action has been confirmed.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ☝ ☝]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 3 was the correct wire and the bomb has changed. The new visible state is display 9, red light, with wire 3 marked CUT; wires 1, 2, 4, and 5 remain red, purple, green, and yellow. Mute sent three ☝ gestures, but their meaning is not established, so I will report them exactly rather than guess.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: wire 3 was correct and the bomb changed. New state: display 9, red light; wire 3 is CUT; wires 1 red, 2 purple, 4 green, 5 yellow. Mute sent ☝ three times; meaning unknown.")
wait()
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is now in a new state: display 9, red light, wire 3 cut, and the other wires unchanged. No new signal from Mute is visible, so I do not know the manual’s instruction for this state. I will ask Mute to send the required wire number using the established repeated-gesture format, rather than have Blind guess.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="For the new display 9 state, please signal the required wire number clearly by repeating the appropriate gesture that many times. I see no new signal yet.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

The visible bomb state remains unchanged, and no gesture from Mute has arrived. I cannot infer a safe wire from the current information, so Blind should not act on a guess. I am requesting the instruction again and asking Blind to wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No gesture arrived. Please resend the manual's required wire number for display 9, using repeated gestures.")
speak(to="blind", text="No new instruction or gesture arrived. Do not cut or manipulate anything yet.")
wait()
```

WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The earlier signal established a counting code: six 🤟 gestures corresponded to display 6, and three 👇 gestures identified wire 3. After the successful cut, Mute sent three ☝ gestures, which most likely identify wire 1 for the new display-9 state. I am sending Blind that inferred instruction now; wire 1 is red.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="For the current display 9 state, Mute's earlier signal was ☝ repeated 3 times. Following the established code, this most likely means wire 1. Wire 1 is red. Verify with the manual and act on wire 1 if confirmed.")
wait()
```

(empty)

The bomb remains unchanged, and there is still no new visible signal from Mute. Blind has already received the inferred instruction to verify and, if supported by the manual, use wire 1. I have no further safe information to add.

```text
wait()
```

DISPLAY [9]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[purple] 3:[CUT] 4:[green] 5:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged: display 9, red light, wire 3 cut, and wire 1 remains red. Mute’s earlier three ☝ gestures are the only available instruction for this state, so I am giving Blind the clearest actionable interpretation: cut wire 1, subject to the manual’s confirmation.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state unchanged. The instruction signal for display 9 was ☝ three times. Cut wire 1, the red wire, if the manual confirms that signal.")

```
